brief: DB reviews last week's FOMC hike and previews this week's Fedspeak. The statement framed the hike as supporting a "timelier return" to 2% and dropped its supply-shock caveat, implying officials will no longer look through inflation, a hawkish shift. The SEP showed 16 officials expecting another 2026 hike, next year split between 50bps and 75bps, and the long-run dot up to 3.2%. Chair Warsh gave no forward guidance, framed the hike as removing a "dose" of accommodation, and cited three drivers of higher long-term rates: economic strength, AI-linked capex and hyperscaler issuance competing for capital, and geopolitics lifting commodity prices. DB expects this week's speakers (Goolsbee, Jefferson, Williams, Barr, Barkin, Hammack, Paulson) to largely echo Warsh, flagging Williams as a possible 2027 easer and Hammack, given her July dissent, as favoring two more hikes this year. DB's baseline is 50bps more tightening to 4.375% by Q1 2027, with 40bps of upside risk given a rising neutral rate, consistent with ~100bps currently priced. Treasury runs a 20-30y buyback (at least $4bn) and Wednesday/Friday data will update the capex outlook.
